## Introduction

This document analyzes classification performance for predictors across different contributor groups. We'll calculate various metrics including AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity, as well as regression statistics.

## Setup

First, we'll load the required libraries and the settings.

```{r load-libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(data.table)
library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse)
library(PRROC)  # For precision-recall curves
library(SummarizedExperiment)
```

## Data Preparation

Load and prepare the proteomics data and prediction results.

```{r load-data}
# Load proteomics data
expdata <- readRDS(PROTEOMICS_RDS)
metadata <- colData(expdata) %>% as.data.frame()

# Load prediction data
pp <- read_predicted_phenotypes(PREDICTED_RDS)
prediction <- get_prediction(pp, "full")

indx = colnames(prediction)%in%c(colnames(prediction)%>%.[grepl("class",.)]%>%gsub("_class.+","",.))
prediction = prediction[,!indx]
# Join metadata and prediction data
data <- metadata %>%
  inner_join(prediction, by = "sample_id")

data = data%>%
  filter(!contributor_code%in%EXCLUDED_CONTRIBUTORS)
data$contributor_code = paste0(data$contributor_code,"_",data$sample_matrix)

data$control =  !rowAnys(data%>%
    select(all_of(c("pd", "als", "ad", "ftd", "stroke")))%>%
    as.matrix() == "1")


```

## Define Analysis Parameters

Identify predictor columns and targets of interest.

```{r define-parameters}

# Identify predictor columns: every predicted-phenotype column, in file order
predictor_names <- intersect(names(data), setdiff(names(prediction), "sample_id"))
predictor_names = setdiff(predictor_names,predictor_names%>%.[grepl("class",.)]%>%gsub("_class.+","",.)%>%unique())
# Define targets of interest (pd and ad in this case)
targets <- c("pd", "als", "ad", "ftd", "stroke")[c(1,3)]  # This is pd and ad
```

## Define Contributor Filters

We create sample groups: all samples, all plasma, and each contributor (site) separately.

```{r define-filters}
# Unique contributor codes (exclude_contributors is empty: none are excluded)
exclude_contributors = NULL
unique_contributors <- unique(data$contributor_code)

# Create a list of filters to apply
# First the pooled groups (all samples; all plasma), then one for each unique contributor
filter_groups <- list(
  all = function(data) filter(data, !contributor_code %in% exclude_contributors),
  all_plasma = function(data) filter(data, !contributor_code %in% c("Q_CSF","U_Serum", "N_CSF","T_CSF"))
)

# Add a filter for each unique contributor code
for (contributor in unique_contributors) {
  filter_name <- paste0("contributor_", contributor)
  # This approach uses force() to evaluate the contributor variable immediately
  filter_groups[[filter_name]] <- local({
    current_contributor <- contributor  # Create a local copy
    force(current_contributor)  # Evaluate immediately
    function(data) {
      filter(data, contributor_code == current_contributor)
    }
  })
}
```

## Define Metric Functions

### Classification Statistics Function

```{r classification-stats-function}
# Function to calculate classification statistics for a single target and predictor
calculate_stats <- function(data, target, predictor, filter_name, filter_func) {
  # Handle data preparation - apply the filter function
  model_data <- filter_func(data) %>%
    select(all_of(c(target, predictor,"control"))) %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(target), ~ replace(.x, .x == -1, NA))) %>%
    drop_na()%>%
    filter((!!sym(target) == 0 & control) | !!sym(target) == 1)%>%
    dplyr::select(-control)
  
  # Skip if there's not enough data or no variation in the target
  if(nrow(model_data) < 10 || length(unique(model_data[[target]])) < 2) {
    return(tibble(
      filter_group = filter_name,
      target = target,
      predictor = predictor,
      accuracy = NA,
      sensitivity = NA,
      specificity = NA,
      auc = NA,
      n = nrow(model_data)
    ))
  }
  
  # Convert target to binary factor (0/1)
  model_data[[target]] <- as.factor(model_data[[target]])
  
  # Calculate AUC directly using pROC
  tryCatch({
    # First check correlation direction
    correlation <- cor(as.numeric(as.character(model_data[[target]])), 
                       model_data[[predictor]], 
                       method = "spearman")
    
    # Create ROC curve with appropriate direction
    roc_obj <- roc(model_data[[target]], model_data[[predictor]], direction = "auto")
    auc_value <- as.numeric(auc(roc_obj))  # Extract the numeric value only
    # Ensure PR curve matches the direction
    if(correlation >= 0) {
      positives <- model_data[[predictor]][model_data[[target]] == "1"]
      negatives <- model_data[[predictor]][model_data[[target]] == "0"]
    } else {
      # Flip for negative correlation
      positives <- -model_data[[predictor]][model_data[[target]] == "1"]
      negatives <- -model_data[[predictor]][model_data[[target]] == "0"]
    }
    

    
    # Calculate PR curve and PR AUC using PRROC package
    # Assuming "1" is the positive class
    pr_curve <- pr.curve(scores.class0 = positives, scores.class1 = negatives, curve = TRUE)
    pr_auc <- pr_curve$auc.integral
    
    # Calculate expected PR-AUC for random classifier (class prevalence)
    positive_prevalence <- sum(model_data[[target]] == "1") / nrow(model_data)
    
    # Find optimal threshold
    optimal_idx <- which.max(roc_obj$sensitivities + roc_obj$specificities - 1)
    optimal_threshold <- roc_obj$thresholds[optimal_idx]
    
    # Calculate classification metrics at optimal threshold
    # After determining correlation direction and optimal threshold
    if(correlation >= 0) {
      # For positive correlation (higher predictor values indicate class "1")
      predicted_class <- ifelse(model_data[[predictor]] >= optimal_threshold, "1", "0")
    } else {
      # For negative correlation (lower predictor values indicate class "1")
      predicted_class <- ifelse(model_data[[predictor]] <= optimal_threshold, "1", "0")
    }

    confusion_matrix <- table(Predicted = predicted_class, Actual = model_data[[target]])
    
    # Calculate metrics from confusion matrix
    if(dim(confusion_matrix)[1] == 2 && dim(confusion_matrix)[2] == 2) {
      tn <- confusion_matrix["0", "0"]
      tp <- confusion_matrix["1", "1"]
      fn <- confusion_matrix["0", "1"]
      fp <- confusion_matrix["1", "0"]
      
      accuracy <- (tp + tn) / (tp + tn + fp + fn)
      sensitivity <- tp / (tp + fn)
      specificity <- tn / (tn + fp)
      
      # Additional metrics
      balanced_accuracy <- (sensitivity + specificity) / 2
      precision <- tp / (tp + fp)
      f1_score <- 2 * (precision * sensitivity) / (precision + sensitivity)
      
      # Calculate Cohen's kappa
      n <- sum(confusion_matrix)
      p_o <- (tp + tn) / n  # observed agreement (accuracy)
      p_e <- ((tp + fp) * (tp + fn) + (tn + fn) * (tn + fp)) / (n * n)  # expected agreement by chance
      kappa <- (p_o - p_e) / (1 - p_e)
    } else {
      # Handle cases where confusion matrix doesn't have expected dimensions
      accuracy <- sum(diag(confusion_matrix)) / sum(confusion_matrix)
      sensitivity <- NA
      specificity <- NA
      balanced_accuracy <- NA
      precision <- NA
      f1_score <- NA
      kappa <- NA
    }
    
    # Return the performance metrics
    tibble(
      filter_group = filter_name,
      target = target,
      predictor = predictor,
      accuracy = accuracy,
      balanced_accuracy = balanced_accuracy,
      sensitivity = sensitivity,
      specificity = specificity,
      precision = precision,
      f1_score = f1_score,
      kappa = kappa,
      auc = auc_value,
      pr_auc = pr_auc,
      random_pr_auc = positive_prevalence,
      pr_auc_lift = pr_auc / positive_prevalence,  # Optional: calculate lift over random
      n = nrow(model_data),
      threshold = optimal_threshold
    )
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Return NAs if calculation fails
    tibble(
      filter_group = filter_name,
      target = target,
      predictor = predictor,
      accuracy = NA,
      balanced_accuracy = NA,
      sensitivity = NA,
      specificity = NA,
      precision = NA,
      f1_score = NA,
      kappa = NA,
      auc = NA,
      pr_auc = NA,
      random_pr_auc = NA,
      pr_auc_lift = NA,
      n = nrow(model_data),
      error = as.character(e)
    )
  })
}
```

### Regression Statistics Function

```{r regression-stats-function}
# Function to calculate regression statistics for a single target and predictor
calculate_regression_stats <- function(data, target, predictor, filter_name, filter_func) {
  # Handle data preparation - apply the filter function
  model_data <- filter_func(data) %>%
    select(all_of(c(target, predictor,"control"))) %>%
    mutate(across(all_of(target), ~ replace(.x, .x == -1, NA))) %>%
    drop_na()%>%
    filter((!!sym(target) == 0 & control) | !!sym(target) == 1)%>%
    dplyr::select(-control)
  
  # Skip if there's not enough data
  if(nrow(model_data) < 10) {
    return(tibble(
      filter_group = filter_name,
      target = target,
      predictor = predictor,
      beta = NA_real_,
      std_error = NA_real_,
      test_statistic = NA_real_,
      test_type = NA_character_,
      df_residual = NA_real_,
      ci_low = NA_real_,
      ci_high = NA_real_,
      odds_ratio = NA_real_,
      or_ci_low = NA_real_,
      or_ci_high = NA_real_,
      p_value = NA_real_,
      regression_type = NA_character_,
      n = nrow(model_data)
    ))
  }
  
    # Standardize variables (z-scoring)
  # For binary targets, only standardize the predictor
  model_data <- model_data %>%
      mutate(across(all_of(predictor), ~ scale(.x)[,1]))

  
  # Run regression
  tryCatch({
    # For binary targets, use logistic regression
    if(all(model_data[[target]] %in% c(0, 1))) {
      # Convert target to numeric to be sure
      model_data[[target]] <- as.numeric(as.character(model_data[[target]]))
      
      # Fit logistic regression model
      model <- glm(
        formula = as.formula(paste(target, "~", predictor)), 
        family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
        data = model_data
      )
      
      # Extract coefficients
      coef_summary <- summary(model)$coefficients
      
      # Extract beta and p-value for the predictor
      beta <- coef_summary[predictor, "Estimate"]
      std_error <- coef_summary[predictor, "Std. Error"]
      z_value <- coef_summary[predictor, "z value"]
      p_value <- coef_summary[predictor, "Pr(>|z|)"]

      # Confidence intervals (Wald-based)
      ci_low <- beta - 1.96 * std_error
      ci_high <- beta + 1.96 * std_error

      # Effect size: odds ratio with CI
      odds_ratio <- exp(beta)
      or_ci_low <- exp(ci_low)
      or_ci_high <- exp(ci_high)

      # Degrees of freedom (residual)
      df_residual <- model$df.residual

      # Return the regression metrics
      tibble(
        filter_group = filter_name,
        target = target,
        predictor = predictor,
        beta = beta,
        std_error = std_error,
        test_statistic = z_value,
        test_type = "z",
        df_residual = df_residual,
        ci_low = ci_low,
        ci_high = ci_high,
        odds_ratio = odds_ratio,
        or_ci_low = or_ci_low,
        or_ci_high = or_ci_high,
        p_value = p_value,
        regression_type = "logistic",
        n = nrow(model_data)
      )
    } else {
      # For continuous targets, use linear regression
      model <- lm(
        formula = as.formula(paste(target, "~", predictor)), 
        data = model_data
      )
      
      # Extract coefficients
      coef_summary <- summary(model)$coefficients
      
      # Extract beta and p-value for the predictor
      beta <- coef_summary[predictor, "Estimate"]
      std_error <- coef_summary[predictor, "Std. Error"]
      t_value <- coef_summary[predictor, "t value"]
      p_value <- coef_summary[predictor, "Pr(>|t|)"]

      # Degrees of freedom and confidence intervals
      df_residual <- model$df.residual
      ci_low <- beta - qt(0.975, df_residual) * std_error
      ci_high <- beta + qt(0.975, df_residual) * std_error

      # Return the regression metrics
      tibble(
        filter_group = filter_name,
        target = target,
        predictor = predictor,
        beta = beta,
        std_error = std_error,
        test_statistic = t_value,
        test_type = "t",
        df_residual = df_residual,
        ci_low = ci_low,
        ci_high = ci_high,
        odds_ratio = NA_real_,
        or_ci_low = NA_real_,
        or_ci_high = NA_real_,
        p_value = p_value,
        regression_type = "linear",
        n = nrow(model_data)
      )
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    # Return NAs if calculation fails
    tibble(
      filter_group = filter_name,
      target = target,
      predictor = predictor,
      beta = NA_real_,
      std_error = NA_real_,
      test_statistic = NA_real_,
      test_type = NA_character_,
      df_residual = NA_real_,
      ci_low = NA_real_,
      ci_high = NA_real_,
      odds_ratio = NA_real_,
      or_ci_low = NA_real_,
      or_ci_high = NA_real_,
      p_value = NA_real_,
      regression_type = NA_character_,
      n = nrow(model_data),
      error = as.character(e)
    )
  })
}
```

## Calculate Statistics

Now we'll calculate statistics for each combination of target, predictor, and filter group.

```{r calculate-stats}
# Create all combinations of targets, predictors, and filter groups
all_combinations <- crossing(
  target = targets,
  predictor = predictor_names,
  filter_info = map(names(filter_groups), function(name) list(name = name, func = filter_groups[[name]]))
)

# Calculate classification statistics for each combination
classification_stats <- pmap_dfr(
  all_combinations,
  function(target, predictor, filter_info) {
    calculate_stats(data, target, predictor, filter_info$name, filter_info$func)
  }
)

# Calculate regression statistics for each combination
regression_stats <- pmap_dfr(
  all_combinations,
  function(target, predictor, filter_info) {
    calculate_regression_stats(data, target, predictor, filter_info$name, filter_info$func)
  }
)

# Combine the statistics - retain all regression columns (test statistic, df, 95% CI)
all_stats <- classification_stats %>%
  left_join(
    regression_stats %>% dplyr::select(filter_group, target, predictor, regression_type,
                                        beta, std_error, test_statistic, test_type,
                                        df_residual, ci_low, ci_high,
                                        odds_ratio, or_ci_low, or_ci_high, p_value),
    by = c("filter_group", "target", "predictor")
  )
```

## Sample Counts by Filter Group

Let's calculate how many samples we have for each filter group.

```{r sample-counts}
# Generate a summary of how many samples per filter group
sample_counts <- data.frame(
  filter_group = character(),
  total_samples = integer(),
  pd_samples = integer(),
  ad_samples = integer(),
  pd_cases = integer(),
  pd_controls = integer(),
  ad_cases = integer(),
  ad_controls = integer(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (filter_name in names(filter_groups)) {
  filtered_data <- filter_groups[[filter_name]](data)
  
  # Count samples for pd
  pd_data <- filtered_data %>% 
    filter(pd != -1) %>%
    mutate(pd = as.factor(pd))
  
  pd_cases <- sum(pd_data$pd == "1", na.rm = TRUE)
  pd_controls <- sum(pd_data$pd == "0", na.rm = TRUE)
  
  # Count samples for ad
  ad_data <- filtered_data %>% 
    filter(ad != -1) %>%
    mutate(ad = as.factor(ad))
  
  ad_cases <- sum(ad_data$ad == "1", na.rm = TRUE)
  ad_controls <- sum(ad_data$ad == "0", na.rm = TRUE)
  
  sample_counts <- rbind(sample_counts, data.frame(
    filter_group = filter_name,
    total_samples = nrow(filtered_data),
    pd_samples = nrow(pd_data),
    ad_samples = nrow(ad_data),
    pd_cases = pd_cases,
    pd_controls = pd_controls,
    ad_cases = ad_cases,
    ad_controls = ad_controls,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ))
}

# Display the sample counts
knitr::kable(sample_counts, caption = "Sample Counts by Contributor Group")
```

```{r save-results}
saveRDS(all_stats, file.path(output_dir, "all_predictor_by_contributor_stats.rds"))

          row.names = FALSE)

          row.names = FALSE)
```

## Results Analysis

Let's create some visualizations of our results.

### Top Predictors by AUC

```{r top-predictors-viz, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
# Filter out NAs and sort by AUC to find top predictors
top_predictors <- all_stats %>%
  filter(!is.na(auc)) %>%
  filter(filter_group == "all") %>%
  group_by(target) %>%
  arrange(desc(auc)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

# Create a plot of top predictors by AUC
ggplot(top_predictors, aes(x = reorder(predictor, auc), y = auc, fill = target)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~target, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Predictors by AUC",
    x = "Predictor",
    y = "AUC"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1")
```

### Performance Metrics by Contributor

```{r contributor-comparison, fig.width=12, fig.height=8}
# Get a subset of predictors for comparison
comparison_predictors <- all_stats %>%
  filter(filter_group == "all") %>%
  group_by(target) %>%
  arrange(desc(auc)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5) %>%
  pull(predictor) %>%
  unique()

# Filter stats for these predictors and all contributors
contributor_comparison <- all_stats %>%
  filter(predictor %in% comparison_predictors) %>%
  filter(!is.na(auc)) %>%
  filter(n >= 20)  # Ensure enough samples

# Plot comparison across contributors
ggplot(contributor_comparison, aes(x = predictor, y = auc, fill = filter_group)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  facet_wrap(~target, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "AUC by Contributor for Top Predictors",
    x = "Predictor",
    y = "AUC",
    fill = "Contributor"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
